movements.heading: Wanting you more than anything else
lines: My dear Lord, you already know what is in me, but I want to say it plainly:
I want you.
More than comfort, more than success, more than a good feeling about my life, I want to belong to you completely.
I want holiness.
I want my will brought into line with yours.
You are the one who put these desires in me, and you are the only one who can satisfy them.
So I bring them back to you.
Make this longing real, steady, and deeper than anything else I chase.
themes: Desire for God above all created goods
Holiness as conformity to God's will
God as the giver and fulfiller of holy desires

scriptures.connection: The psalm gives language to a soul that is not merely seeking relief but seeking God himself. It supports the prayer’s central longing for communion with God as the deepest desire of the heart.
Paul teaches that God works in his people both to will and to work for his good pleasure. This grounds the confession that holy desires come from God and must be fulfilled by God’s own power.

movements.heading: Asking to be changed from the inside
lines: I want real fellowship with you, not just thoughts about you.
I want the sin still living in me to be put to death, especially the pride that can hide inside spiritual things.
Keep me from admiring my own growth, my own prayers, or my own experiences.
Give me a clear, tender understanding of what true godliness is.
Show me the beauty of holiness
not as a religious performance, but as a life shaped by Christ.
themes: Communion with God
Mortification of remaining sin
Spiritual pride as a subtle corruption
True godliness centered on Christ and expressed in holiness

scriptures.connection: This passage connects life in the Spirit with putting to death the deeds of the body. It supports the prayer’s request for real inward change rather than surface religion.
James warns that God opposes the proud and gives grace to the humble. This speaks directly to the prayer’s concern over spiritual pride, especially pride disguised as devotion.
Paul describes the mystery of godliness in relation to Christ himself. This helps frame godliness not as vague moral improvement, but as life rooted in and shaped by the revealed Christ.

movements.heading: Becoming more like you
lines: Lord, how good it would be to reflect you as much as a creature can reflect the Creator.
I know I will never be God, and I do not want to pretend otherwise.
But I do want more of your likeness
more purity, more love, more steadiness, more obedience.
Stretch my heart so there is more room for holiness.
Pull my life more fully toward you, so I live less for myself and more for your honour.
themes: Creaturely likeness to God without collapsing Creator and creature
Growth in holiness
Living for God’s glory rather than self

scriptures.connection: Peter calls believers to holiness because God is holy. This supports the prayer’s desire to be like God in the way Scripture commands: not by becoming divine, but by sharing in a holy pattern of life.
Paul describes believers being transformed into the image of the Lord. This grounds the request for increasing likeness to God as an ongoing work of grace.

movements.heading: Not settling for spiritual experiences
lines: When you give me sweet moments of prayer, peace, or closeness with you, do not let me turn those gifts into something I admire in myself.
And when I feel settled after meeting with you, remind me that I still know so little, love so little, and obey so imperfectly.
Keep me grateful, but keep me hungry.
Let every taste of your goodness make me want more of you, not make me satisfied with myself.
themes: Spiritual experiences as gifts, not grounds for self-satisfaction
Humility after communion with God
Pressing on in faith and obedience

scriptures.connection: Paul refuses to treat his spiritual progress as though he has already arrived, and instead presses on toward Christ. This supports the prayer’s refusal to settle for past experiences or present comfort.

Paul reminds believers that everything they have is received, not self-produced. This speaks to the danger of becoming pleased with one’s spiritual experiences as though they were personal achievements.

movements.heading: Coming close when my heart feels weak
lines: Draw me nearer to you.
Teach me to love you, to long for you, to ask boldly, to keep coming back, and not to give up when prayer feels like wrestling.
I need deliverance from the sin that still clings to me.
My heart wanders.
My affections grow dull.
It grieves me that I can lose sight of you, my beloved Lord, even after knowing your kindness.
Bring me back again and again.
themes: Persevering prayer
The ongoing struggle with indwelling sin
Spiritual dullness and wandering
Grief over losing sight of Christ

scriptures.connection: Jesus teaches his disciples to pray always and not lose heart. This supports the prayer’s language of pleading, wrestling, and continuing to seek God when the soul feels weak.

Paul gives voice to the believer’s painful awareness of remaining sin and the cry for deliverance through Jesus Christ. This closely matches the prayer’s longing to be freed from the “body of sin.”},{

movements.heading: Held in love and ready for whatever you give
lines: Wrap my whole life in your love.
Keep me wanting you
not only in strong moments, but in ordinary days, tired days, and painful days.
Make me humble.
Make me willing to receive your will instead of fighting for my own.
Fix my eyes more firmly on you, so I am better prepared to serve when you call me to act, and better prepared to endure when you call me to suffer.
themes: Life held in divine love
Humble surrender to God’s will
Being formed for obedience and suffering
Steadfast focus on God

scriptures.connection: Paul calls believers to offer themselves to God and be transformed so they may discern his will. This supports the prayer’s desire for humble surrender and a life increasingly directed toward God.

Peter teaches believers who suffer according to God’s will to entrust themselves to the faithful Creator while doing good. This directly supports the prayer’s closing request to be fitted both for doing and for suffering.

Jude calls believers to keep themselves in the love of God while continuing in faith and prayer. This illuminates the prayer’s desire to have the whole life held within divine love and ongoing longing for God.

provenance.originalAuthor: Unattributed Puritan source (compiled and edited by Arthur Bennett)
provenance.originalSource: The Valley of Vision: A Collection of Puritan Prayers and Devotions, ed. Arthur Bennett (The Banner of Truth Trust)
provenance.copyrightStatus: Compilation, titles and arrangement in copyright (Banner of Truth, 1975); underlying Puritan sources are public domain.
provenance.adaptationNote: Contemporary prayer based on the theological themes and ideas of the historical source; not a reproduction of the original wording.

movements.heading: Longing to be what pleases you
lines: My God, it feels like a taste of heaven simply to please you and to become the person you want me to be.
I want to be holy because you are holy.
I want the purity of Christ to shape me.
I want your Spirit to make me whole and mature in every part of me.
Your commands are not a burden to me;
they are beautiful.
So why do I keep resisting them?
Why do I still break what I know is good?
themes: God’s holiness as the standard and desire of the believer
Delight in obedience
Longing for sanctification and moral purity

scriptures.connection: Peter calls Christians to holiness because God himself is holy, grounding the believer’s moral life in God’s own character rather than in mere rule-keeping.
John teaches that love for God changes how his commandments are viewed; they are not meant to be hated burdens but the path of loving obedience.

movements.heading: Grieving that I sin against such kindness
lines: I am deeply sorry that I am still a sinner, and that my sin grieves you
the God who has shown me nothing but goodness, mercy, and grace.
If you only punished me, that would be terrible;
but what cuts me even deeper is that I offend you while you keep answering me with kindness.
I sin again and again, and still you do not stop being patient and generous toward me.
themes: Conviction of sin
God’s patience and kindness toward sinners
Grieving God rather than treating sin lightly

scriptures.connection: Paul warns believers not to grieve the Holy Spirit, showing that sin is not merely rule-breaking but a personal offense against the God who has sealed his people.
Paul says God’s kindness is meant to lead to repentance; this supports the prayer’s grief that divine mercy, not only judgment, exposes the ugliness of sin.

movements.heading: Wanting my life to honor you
lines: At times I think I could endure almost any suffering if only I did not dishonor you.
How can I treat lightly the glory of the God who is so good?
Teach me what it means, today and every day, to glorify you and worship you with my actual life
not only with my words.
themes: God’s worthiness to be glorified
Worship expressed in daily life
Desire to honor God above comfort

scriptures.connection: Paul applies God’s glory to ordinary actions, showing that worship is not limited to formal religious moments but includes the whole shape of daily life.
Paul presents the believer’s body and life as a living sacrifice, which directly supports the prayer’s desire for practical, embodied worship.

movements.heading: Giving myself wholly to you
lines: I want to hand over my whole self to you
my soul, my body, my plans, my time, my desires, without holding anything back.
Keep me from trying to belong to myself.
Bend my will toward yours.
Train my loves until they agree with your love.
I do not want a private corner of my heart where I still insist on being my own master.
themes: Consecration of the whole person to God
Belonging to God rather than self
Surrender of will and affections

scriptures.connection: Paul reminds believers that they are not their own because they were bought with a price, grounding the prayer’s desire to stop claiming ownership over oneself.
Paul describes Christian life as no longer centered on the self but lived by faith in Christ, which fits the prayer’s longing to have the will and life reshaped by God.

movements.heading: Joining the worship you deserve
lines: And yet, Lord, I know I still cannot live in this world without sin.
I hate that reality, and I do not want to make peace with it.
Let the angels praise you without stopping.
Let all heaven bow low before you, the blessed King.
I long to join their worship, now and forever.
But even if I praised you for all eternity, I would still only be giving you a tiny part of the honor you deserve.
So please give me a heart filled with your own heavenly love
love that worships you gladly and belongs to you completely.
themes: Ongoing struggle with remaining sin
Heavenly worship
God’s infinite worthiness
Need for divine love to fill the heart

scriptures.connection: John refuses the claim that believers are already without sin, while also directing them to honest confession and God’s faithful forgiveness.
John’s vision of countless heavenly beings worshiping the Lamb gives biblical shape to the prayer’s longing to join the angels in unending praise.
Paul says God’s love is poured into believers’ hearts through the Holy Spirit, supporting the final request for a heart filled with divine love.

provenance.originalAuthor: Unattributed Puritan source (compiled and edited by Arthur Bennett)
provenance.originalSource: The Valley of Vision: A Collection of Puritan Prayers and Devotions, ed. Arthur Bennett (The Banner of Truth Trust)
provenance.copyrightStatus: Compilation, titles and arrangement in copyright (Banner of Truth, 1975); underlying Puritan sources are public domain.
provenance.adaptationNote: Contemporary prayer based on the theological themes and ideas of the historical source; not a reproduction of the original wording.

movements.heading: Resting in your untroubled rule
lines: God Most High, you are never overwhelmed.
I come to you worn out, tangled up, and carrying more than I can manage, but you are perfectly at peace.
Nothing you plan is at risk of failing.
Nothing can limit your power, and your goodness never runs dry.
You can take confusion and make it serve your wise purpose.
Even what feels like defeat in my life is not outside your rule.
You reign, and that steadies me.
themes: God’s sovereign rule over all things
God’s perfect peace and unthreatened purposes
God’s power and goodness in the middle of human confusion

scriptures.connection: God declares that his purpose will stand and that he will accomplish what he intends. This grounds the prayer’s confidence that God’s plans are not anxious, fragile, or uncertain.

Paul teaches that God works all things together for good for those who love him. That supports the prayer’s trust that even painful confusion and apparent defeats are not wasted under God’s providence.

movements.heading: Bringing you my sins and burdens
lines: So I come as I really am:
a sinner with worries, griefs, and responsibilities I cannot carry rightly on my own.
I place every concern in your hands.
I also bring every sin into the light, because I have no answer for my guilt except the blood of Jesus.
Father, do not let me hide from you.
Let me come honestly, trusting your mercy instead of pretending I am clean.
themes: Honest confession of sin
Casting cares on God
Cleansing through Christ’s blood

scriptures.connection: Peter calls believers to humble themselves under God’s hand and cast their anxieties on him because he cares for them. This directly supports bringing burdens to God instead of trying to control them alone.

John connects walking in the light with cleansing through Jesus’ blood and God’s faithfulness to forgive confessed sin. This grounds the prayer’s refusal to hide sin and its confidence in Christ’s atonement.

movements.heading: Staying close to my Shepherd
lines: Please wake up my heart again.
Make my faith more than ideas I can explain.
Bring me close to Jesus, my Shepherd.
Train my ears to know his voice, to recognize what is true, and to follow where he calls, even when obedience costs me something.
themes: Spiritual renewal
Christ as Shepherd
Obedient faith that hears and follows Christ

scriptures.connection: Jesus describes his sheep as those who hear his voice, know him, and follow him, while he gives them eternal life. This is the clearest biblical grounding for the prayer’s desire to live near the Shepherd and respond to his call.

Hebrews speaks of mature believers having their powers of discernment trained by practice. This supports the request for a faith that is not merely theoretical but shaped by lived obedience and spiritual discernment.

movements.heading: Keeping me in truth by your Spirit
lines: Keep me from being fooled by lies, especially the ones that sound close to the truth.
Hold me in your Word.
Keep me from spiritual harm by teaching me to walk in the strength and guidance of the Holy Spirit.
Give me a deeper, steadier trust in what is eternal.
Let the truths I know become things I have learned with my whole life, not just stored in my mind.
themes: Protection from deception
Abiding in truth
The Spirit’s guidance and empowering presence
Faith becoming lived experience

scriptures.connection: Jesus says the Spirit of truth will guide his people into truth and glorify Christ. This supports the prayer’s dependence on the Spirit to keep the believer from deception and centered on Christ.
Paul calls believers to walk by the Spirit in their struggle against the flesh. This grounds the prayer’s request to be kept from harm not by self-reliance but by the Spirit’s active help.

movements.heading: Standing with the gospel without shame
lines: Do not let me be embarrassed by the gospel.
If following Jesus brings misunderstanding, rejection, or contempt, help me not to shrink back.
Give me courage to speak for the truth without pride or harshness.
Keep showing me that Jesus is the heart of the gospel, and that any real power in my witness comes from your Spirit, not from my cleverness or confidence.
themes: Boldness in the gospel
Sharing in Christ’s reproach
Christ as the center of the gospel
Dependence on the Spirit rather than human ability

scriptures.connection: Paul says he is not ashamed of the gospel because it is God’s power for salvation. This directly supports the prayer’s desire to stand openly with the gospel and trust its divine power.

Paul urges Timothy not to be ashamed of testimony about the Lord and to share in suffering for the gospel by God’s power. This fits the prayer’s request for courage to bear reproach without shrinking back.

Paul centers his message on Christ crucified and rejects reliance on impressive human wisdom so that faith rests on God’s power. This supports the prayer’s focus on Jesus as the essence of the gospel and the Spirit as the source of power.

movements.heading: Asking you to uproot what is cold and false in me
lines: Lord, help me.
I am often colder toward you than I want to admit.
My unbelief weakens my confidence, and my sin makes me forget you.
Do not just trim the visible parts of what is wrong in me;
pull sin up by the roots.
Teach me that I am only truly alive when I live for you, and that everything else, if it is cut off from you, is small and passing.
Only your presence can make me holy, devoted, strong, and genuinely glad.
Stay with me, gracious God, and make your home in me.
themes: Confession of spiritual coldness
Unbelief and sin as threats to fellowship with God
Deep repentance and sanctification
True life found in living for God
God’s presence as the source of holiness, strength, and joy

scriptures.connection: David asks God for a clean heart, renewed spirit, restored joy, and sustaining grace after sin. This supports the prayer’s plea for inward renewal rather than surface-level improvement.
Paul describes the Christian life as being crucified with Christ and living by faith in the Son of God. This grounds the prayer’s claim that true life is life lived to God through Christ.
Jesus teaches that his disciples can bear fruit only by abiding in him. This supports the prayer’s closing dependence on God’s presence for holiness, strength, and spiritual fruitfulness.

provenance.originalAuthor: Unattributed Puritan source (compiled and edited by Arthur Bennett)
provenance.originalSource: The Valley of Vision: A Collection of Puritan Prayers and Devotions, ed. Arthur Bennett (The Banner of Truth Trust)
provenance.copyrightStatus: Compilation, titles and arrangement in copyright (Banner of Truth, 1975); underlying Puritan sources are public domain.
provenance.adaptationNote: Contemporary prayer based on the theological themes and ideas of the historical source; not a reproduction of the original wording.

movements.heading: Finding my deepest joy in knowing you
lines: Father, you are the goal my life was made for.
My richest joy is not simply to know things about you, but to know you
and to see myself honestly before you.
When my mind, desires, emotions, and choices are all turned toward you, I feel most awake.
Time with you is never wasted.
There is no better use of my hours than honest fellowship with you and a truthful look at my own heart in your presence.
themes: God is the final purpose of human life.
True self-knowledge happens before God, not apart from him.
Communion with God is the believer’s deepest pleasure and highest good.

scriptures.connection: Jesus describes eternal life in terms of knowing the only true God and Jesus Christ whom he has sent. That grounds the prayer’s claim that knowing God is not a side interest but the heart of real life.
David’s single great desire is to dwell with the Lord and behold his beauty. This supports the longing for communion with God as the believer’s highest delight.

movements.heading: Wanting my whole self to move toward you
lines: Draw every part of me into the pursuit of you.
I want my thoughts, loves, habits, and longings to stop pulling in different directions and to become united in wanting you.
Make me more like you.
Teach me to want holiness, not as a performance, but because I want you yourself and the joy of being near you without hiding.
themes: The Christian life involves the whole person being turned toward God.
Holiness is conformity to God and grows out of love for him.
The believer longs not only for God’s gifts but for God himself.

scriptures.connection: Paul teaches that believers are transformed into the likeness of the Lord as they behold his glory. This directly supports the prayer’s desire for conformity to God through fellowship with him.
The psalm portrays the soul thirsting for God himself and clinging to him. It gives biblical language to the prayer’s longing for full enjoyment of God.

movements.heading: Watching my heart because I love you
lines: Give me a careful and tender spirit toward you.
Let me be more afraid of grieving you than of losing comfort, praise, convenience, or control.
You are not a distant judge to me;
you are my blessed God, my Father, and my friend.
Because I love you, I want to please you.
Guard me from making peace with anything in me that offends you.
themes: Holy watchfulness is part of sincere love for God.
Sin matters because it grieves the God who has loved and adopted us.
The fear of offending God is not servile terror but reverent love.

scriptures.connection: Paul warns believers not to grieve the Holy Spirit, especially in the context of putting away sinful patterns. This supports the prayer’s concern to avoid offending God out of love.
Because believers have God’s promises, Paul calls them to cleanse themselves and pursue holiness in the fear of God. The verse connects reverence, watchfulness, and practical holiness.

movements.heading: Wanting your glory more than self-centered happiness
lines: Lord, teach me to measure joy by whether you are honored and delighted in, not by whether I am comfortable or admired.
I do not want to chase a happiness that leaves you out.
Make it my highest ambition to glorify you, to enjoy you, and to be glad that you are seen as worthy.
themes: Human joy is rightly ordered when it is rooted in God’s glory.
The Christian’s ambition is to honor God above self-centered satisfaction.
Delighting in God and glorifying God belong together.

scriptures.connection: Paul gives the broad principle that even ordinary actions should be done for God’s glory. This grounds the prayer’s desire for all joy and ambition to be God-centered.
Paul’s hope is that Christ would be honored in his body whether by life or death, because Christ is his life and gain. This supports the prayer’s preference for God’s honor above personal comfort.

movements.heading: Putting all my life in your hands
lines: I want all my time to belong to you
at home, on the road, in work, in rest, in conversations, and in hidden moments no one else sees.
I place my worries, plans, responsibilities, and desires into your hands.
Make me willing to be fully at your disposal.
Free me from the need to run my life as though it were my own private kingdom.
themes: Every place and circumstance can be lived before God.
Surrender means entrusting concerns and plans to God’s wise rule.
The believer belongs to the Lord in life’s ordinary details.

scriptures.connection: Paul says believers do not live or die to themselves but belong to the Lord. This supports the prayer’s surrender of time, plans, and personal claims to God.
Paul calls Christians to do everything in the name of the Lord Jesus with gratitude to God. That gives biblical shape to offering ordinary life—home, travel, work, and speech—to God.

movements.heading: Making you my only end
lines: Help me live to you forever.
Be the final reason behind what I choose, what I refuse, what I love, and what I become.
Kill the sinful self-love in me that wants your gifts without your rule.
Let me not protect, excuse, or feed that old selfish life even in one small corner.
Make me yours
gladly, wholly, and without reserve.
themes: God is the believer’s final end and supreme allegiance.
Sanctification includes the putting to death of sinful self-rule.
Christian surrender is whole-life devotion, not partial religious interest.

scriptures.connection: Paul describes the Christian life as no longer centered on the self but lived by faith in the Son of God who loved and gave himself for us. This supports the prayer’s desire to live wholly to God rather than to the sinful self.
Jesus calls his disciples to deny themselves, take up their cross daily, and follow him. This grounds the prayer’s strong language about rejecting sinful self-love and yielding entirely to God.

movements.heading: Recognizing that everything I have comes from you
lines: Great I AM, everything I have is from you.
My life, my breath, every good thing I enjoy, every step forward, every ordinary ability to see, hear, touch, think, love, and receive beauty
all of it is your gift.
Nothing that makes life good or meaningful comes from me first.
I receive it from your hand.
themes: God is the source and giver of life and every good gift.
Human life is dependent on God not only for spiritual blessings but for ordinary created gifts.
Thanksgiving begins by acknowledging that nothing good is self-produced.

scriptures.connection: Paul tells the Athenians that God gives life, breath, and everything, and that all people live and move in him. This directly supports the prayer’s confession that even ordinary existence and ability are received from God.
James grounds every good gift in the unchanging generosity of God. This helps frame happiness, beauty, truth, and daily provision as gifts rather than possessions earned or owned independently.

movements.heading: Owning my need for your grace
lines: And in my life with you, I am just as dependent
completely dependent.
Please give me the grace to see how much I need grace.
Show me my sin honestly, so I will not hide it or defend it.
Show me my weakness, so I will stop pretending I am strong on my own and learn to find my strength in you.
themes: Grace is needed even to recognize the need for grace.
True self-knowledge before God includes both sin and weakness.
God’s strength is known most deeply by those who stop relying on themselves.

scriptures.connection: Jesus teaches that apart from him his disciples can do nothing. This grounds the prayer’s confession of total spiritual dependence rather than self-sufficiency.
Paul learns that Christ’s power is made perfect in weakness. This supports the request to understand personal weakness not as the end of hope, but as the place where God’s strength is known.

movements.heading: Confessing the sin I would rather excuse
lines: Thank you for any real sorrow over sin that is already in me.
Please deepen it.
My sin is not light or harmless;
it runs deeper than I like to admit.
It comes from a heart that can be hard, proud, and quick to justify itself.
Help me confess without making excuses, without presenting myself as better than I am, and without pretending I have earned anything from you.
Let my repentance be honest, grieving, and humble before you.
themes: Sin is serious and rooted in the heart, not merely in outward actions.
Repentance is itself a gift from God and should be desired more deeply.
Confession rejects self-justification and comes to God without claims of merit.

scriptures.connection: David’s confession shows sin as first and finally an offense before God, not something to minimize or excuse. It gives biblical shape to honest repentance that appeals to mercy rather than merit.
This passage shows that God receives a broken and contrite heart rather than religious performance used as a cover. It supports the prayer’s desire for genuine sorrow instead of self-defense.
John warns against denying sin and holds out God’s faithful forgiveness to those who confess. This supports both the honesty of confession and the hope that confession is not hopeless despair.

movements.heading: Asking you to heal what is sick in me
lines: I need healing, not just improvement.
Good Physician, there is more than enough in me for you to work on.
Come near and show your power where I am diseased by sin, pride, unbelief, and self-reliance.
Do in me what I cannot do for myself.
themes: Sin is not only guilt but spiritual sickness needing divine healing.
God’s saving power reaches people who cannot cure themselves.
The image of God as physician expresses both mercy and authority.

scriptures.connection: Jesus identifies himself as the physician who comes for sinners rather than the self-righteous. This directly grounds the prayer’s appeal for healing from the one who came to call and restore the spiritually sick.
Jeremiah asks the Lord for healing and salvation together, recognizing that restoration must come from God. This supports the prayer’s cry for God to heal what the worshiper cannot repair.

movements.heading: Strengthening the faith you have given me
lines: I need faith, and even that has come from you.
Please keep it alive, make it stronger, and grow it deeper.
Fix my trust on the finished work of the Savior, on the greatness and fatherly majesty of the Father, and on the living work of the Spirit in me.
Work in me now, so that I do not treat you as doubtful or unreliable, but trust you as the true, powerful, and faithful God you are.
themes: Faith is a gift from God and must be sustained by God.
Christian faith is centered on Christ’s saving work and lived before the triune God.
Trust grows as God reveals himself as truthful, mighty, and faithful.

scriptures.connection: Paul teaches that salvation by grace through faith is God’s gift, not a ground for boasting. This supports the prayer’s request that God maintain and increase the very faith he has given.
Believers are called to look to Jesus, the founder and perfecter of faith. This grounds the prayer’s desire to have faith centered on the Savior’s work rather than on the believer’s own stability.

Peter frames Christian life in relation to the Father’s foreknowledge, the Spirit’s sanctifying work, and obedience to Jesus Christ. This supports the prayer’s explicitly Trinitarian orientation without forcing a later formula onto the text.

movements.heading: Bringing back to you the fruit you grow in me
lines: Then I can come to you with a heart full of love, gratitude, hope, and joy.
And even those are not my achievements;
they are fruit from your own garden.
Let me lay them at your feet.

Teach me to love you with a love that does not grow cold, to trust you with a confidence that does not collapse, to hope in you with expectation that does not fade, and to delight in you with joy that cannot be smothered.
Use the best of me to honor you.
Let my life catch and reflect something of your own glory.
themes: Love, gratitude, hope, and joy are fruits of God’s work in the believer, not grounds for boasting.
The proper end of spiritual growth is worship and the glorifying of God.
Believers reflect God’s glory as they are transformed by him.

scriptures.connection: Paul describes love, joy, and related virtues as the fruit of the Spirit rather than self-generated moral achievement. This supports the image of bringing God the fruit that he himself has grown.

Jesus connects abiding in him with bearing fruit, glorifying the Father, remaining in his love, and receiving his joy. This passage closely supports the prayer’s movement from dependence to fruitfulness, love, joy, and God’s glory.
Paul describes believers being transformed as they behold the Lord’s glory. This grounds the prayer’s desire to reflect God’s glory rather than merely perform religious devotion.

movements.heading: Trusting what you have promised in Christ
lines: Glorious Lord, my covenant God, you do not make empty promises.
Everything you have promised finds its yes in Jesus, and you will bring every word of yours to pass.
What you have spoken will stand.
What you have purposed will happen.
Help me begin there, not with my fears, not with what I can see, but with your faithful character.
themes: God’s covenant faithfulness
the certainty of God’s promises in Christ
God’s trustworthy word and sovereign purpose

scriptures.connection: Paul teaches that God’s promises are secured and confirmed in Christ, which directly grounds the prayer’s confidence that what God has promised will be fulfilled.
This passage presents God as the one whose counsel stands and whose purposes are accomplished, supporting the prayer’s trust that God’s spoken will cannot fail.

movements.heading: Confessing how often I have lived as if you were not enough
lines: Father, I have not always lived like I believe this.
I have doubted you.
At times I have acted as though you were distant, unreal, or not worth trusting.
Forgive me for that kind of living death
when I have tried to make a life for myself apart from you, and when I have been satisfied with things that fade almost as soon as I hold them.
themes: confession of unbelief
the emptiness of life apart from God
repentance from finding satisfaction in temporary things

scriptures.connection: God rebukes his people for forsaking him, the fountain of living waters, and turning to broken substitutes. That captures the prayer’s confession of seeking life and contentment apart from God.
This verse grounds the prayer’s appeal for forgiveness, assuring believers that honest confession is met by God’s faithful cleansing.

movements.heading: Resting my pardon on Jesus
lines: Thank you that your grace has not left me there.
You have brought me back to repentance.
You have taught me to see my forgiveness in the wounds of Jesus.
My hope is not in how strongly I feel or how well I perform, but in him
God come near in human flesh, my life’s foundation, and the source of every hope I have.
themes: grace leading to repentance
forgiveness through Christ’s wounds
Christ incarnate as the ground of life and hope

scriptures.connection: Peter connects Christ’s wounds with the believer’s healing from sin, supporting the prayer’s language of reading pardon in the wounds of Jesus.
John’s testimony that the Word became flesh grounds the prayer’s confession of Jesus as God incarnate, the one in whom God’s grace is personally revealed.
Paul says that no foundation can be laid other than Jesus Christ, which supports the prayer’s dependence on Christ as the ground of life and hope.

movements.heading: Learning to want your will
lines: Teach me to yield to your will without resentment.
Make your ways good to me, not just right in theory.
Train my heart to love what you command, and to stop treating my own will as wiser than yours.
Help me believe that, for your child, nothing you do is careless, wasted, or cruel, even when I cannot understand it.
themes: surrender to God’s will
delighting in God’s law
trusting God’s fatherly goodness in all circumstances

scriptures.connection: The psalmist speaks of delighting to do God’s will and having God’s law within the heart, which fits the prayer’s desire not merely to obey but to love God’s commands.
Paul assures believers that God works all things together for good for those who love him and are called according to his purpose, grounding the prayer’s confidence in God’s good providence.

movements.heading: Leaving my troubles in your hands
lines: Help me put my concerns into your hands instead of trying to control everything myself.
You are not threatened by evil, and you are never trapped by it.
Without approving of sin or being stained by it, you are able to overrule even dark and painful things and carry forward your good purposes until all you intend is complete.
themes: God’s sovereignty over evil
providence without making God the author of sin
trusting God with burdens and outcomes

scriptures.connection: Joseph tells his brothers that what they meant for evil, God meant for good. This supports the prayer’s trust that God can govern evil actions toward his saving purposes without excusing the evil itself.
Peter calls believers to humble themselves under God’s mighty hand and cast their anxieties on him, which directly supports leaving concerns in God’s care.

movements.heading: Asking for faith that holds steady in trials
lines: Give me faith like Abraham’s
faith that does not collapse when your promise seems impossible.
When trouble comes, keep me from trying to teach you how to run my life.
Instead, help me honor you in the middle of it.
Grow me in the life you have given me.
Lift me out of the fog of doubt and fear, and set my feet on the high ground of security in Christ.
Teach me simply to believe that you cannot lie, and that you will not abandon your purpose.
themes: faith in God’s promises
growth in the Christian life
assurance and security in Christ
glorifying God through trials

scriptures.connection: Paul describes Abraham as strengthened in faith because he was fully convinced God could do what he promised. This is the explicit biblical background for asking for Abraham-like faith.
James teaches that trials test faith and produce steadfastness, supporting the prayer’s request to glorify God in trials and advance in spiritual maturity through them.
Hebrews anchors Christian encouragement in God’s unchangeable purpose and the impossibility of God lying, matching the prayer’s confidence that God cannot deceive or turn aside from his purpose.

movements.heading: Praising the one who is worthy of my confidence
lines: Give me the confidence I should have in Jesus
the confidence due to the one who is faithful, worthy of praise, and blessed forever.
Let my life answer your promises with trust.
Amen.
themes: confidence in Christ
praise and worship
faith answering God’s faithfulness

scriptures.connection: Paul’s doxology speaks of Christ as God over all, blessed forever, which supports the prayer’s closing praise of Jesus as worthy of confidence and worship.
The heavenly worship of the Lamb shows Christ’s worthiness to receive praise, reinforcing the prayer’s final appeal to trust and honor him.

provenance.originalAuthor: Unattributed Puritan source (compiled and edited by Arthur Bennett)
provenance.originalSource: The Valley of Vision: A Collection of Puritan Prayers and Devotions, ed. Arthur Bennett (The Banner of Truth Trust)
provenance.copyrightStatus: Compilation, titles and arrangement in copyright (Banner of Truth, 1975); underlying Puritan sources are public domain.
provenance.adaptationNote: Contemporary prayer based on the theological themes and ideas of the historical source; not a reproduction of the original wording.

movements.heading: Amazed by the help you have given me
lines: Eternal Father, your love is astonishing.
You gave your Son to suffer in my place.
You have given your Spirit to teach me, comfort me, and lead me.
You even send your unseen servants to care for me in ways I usually never notice.
I am small, weak, and undeserving, and yet heaven itself is at work for my good.
Help me not to take that mercy lightly.
themes: The Father’s love shown in sending the Son
Christ suffering in the sinner’s place
The Holy Spirit as teacher, comforter, and guide
God’s unseen care through angels
Grace toward the weak and undeserving

scriptures.connection: Paul argues from the Father’s gift of his own Son to the certainty of God’s continuing generosity toward his people. This supports the prayer’s amazement that salvation and ongoing help come from God’s undeserved love.
Jesus promises the Holy Spirit as the Helper who teaches and reminds his disciples of his words. That directly grounds the request to be taught, comforted, and guided by the Spirit.
Hebrews describes angels as servants sent by God for the sake of those who inherit salvation. This supports the prayer’s confidence that God may use unseen servants for the believer’s welfare.

movements.heading: Asking you to keep helping me until the fight is over
lines: Please keep your unseen servants active for me according to your will.
Let them rejoice whenever your grace grows in me.
Do not let your help toward me stop until my struggle is finished and, by your mercy, I stand safely with you at the end.
themes: Perseverance in the Christian life
God’s heavenly care for believers
Grace growing in the believer
Final salvation after spiritual conflict

scriptures.connection: Jesus says there is joy before the angels of God over one sinner who repents. This supports the prayer’s picture of heaven rejoicing when grace advances in a person.
Paul expresses confidence that God will complete the good work he began in believers. This grounds the prayer’s request that God continue his help until the believer reaches the end.

Jude praises God as the one able to keep his people from stumbling and present them blameless before his glory. That directly supports the hope of standing safely and victoriously before God at the end.

movements.heading: Being honest about what is wrong in me
lines: Father, I know how easily I lean toward evil.
I can be strangely lifeless toward what is good.
I resist the Spirit’s prompting more than I want to admit.
Please do not give me over to myself.
Let my stubborn heart move you to mercy, not to cast me away.
Have pity on me, and keep working in me until I am truly changed.
themes: Confession of remaining sin
Spiritual deadness and resistance to the Spirit
Dependence on God’s persevering mercy
The Father’s compassion toward weak children

scriptures.connection: The psalm presents God as a compassionate Father who remembers the frailty of his people. This supports the prayer’s appeal that weakness and hardness would awaken mercy rather than abandonment.

Paul warns believers not to grieve the Holy Spirit, showing that resistance to the Spirit is a real danger in the Christian life. The verse also places that warning within the security of being sealed for redemption.
David asks God for a clean heart, a renewed spirit, and the continued presence of the Holy Spirit after grievous sin. This matches the prayer’s plea not to be abandoned but renewed from within.

movements.heading: When the enemy uses my sin against me
lines: When my own corruption gives the enemy an opening, show that your power is greater than all the powers against me.
Let it be plain that heaven is stronger than hell, and that those who are for me are more than those who are against me.
Come to my help with all the riches of your covenant mercy.
Keep me feeding on your strengthening Word.
Teach me to search the Scriptures not just for information, but to find you there.
themes: Spiritual warfare against the enemy, the world, and the flesh
God’s superior power and protection
Covenant mercy as the believer’s help
Scripture as nourishment and the place where God makes himself known

scriptures.connection: John encourages believers that the one in them is greater than the one in the world. This directly supports the prayer’s confidence that God’s power is greater than the enemy’s advantage.

Elisha’s servant is shown that the heavenly host surrounding them is greater than the visible enemy army. This illuminates the prayer’s language that those for God’s people are greater than those against them.
Paul teaches that Scripture makes people wise for salvation and equips them for every good work. This supports the request to be strengthened and trained through God’s Word.
Jesus confronts people who study Scripture yet miss the life found in him. This supports the prayer’s desire to search Scripture in order to meet God, not merely to gain religious knowledge.

movements.heading: Receiving your correction as a child
lines: If my wandering brings your correction, help me receive it with humility.
Teach me not to resent your hand, but to trust the love behind it.
Show me what you are exposing.
Make me quick to return, quick to obey, and quick to do again what love for you requires.
Let every fatherly dealing make me share more deeply in your holiness.
themes: Fatherly discipline
Repentance and return to first obedience
God’s correction as loving rather than cruel
Sanctification through discipline

scriptures.connection: Hebrews teaches that God disciplines his children for their good, so that they may share his holiness. This is the clearest biblical foundation for receiving correction as the Father’s loving work.
Jesus calls the church in Ephesus to repent and do the works they did at first. This supports the prayer’s request to respond promptly and return to the obedience love once produced.

movements.heading: Letting every fall and trial drive me nearer to you
lines: When I fall, let it push me lower onto my knees instead of deeper into hiding.
And when you lift me up, let me rise with a truer, stronger devotion to you.
Make every cross holy in its effect on me.
Turn every loss into real gain.
Make every “no” from you a spiritual advantage.
Let every dark day become a place where the Holy Spirit gives light, and every night of testing become, by your grace, a song to you.
themes: Repentance after failure
God sanctifying suffering and loss
Growth in devotion through trial
The Holy Spirit giving light in darkness
Joy and praise produced by grace even in testing

scriptures.connection: Paul teaches that God works all things for the good of those who love him, specifically conforming them to the image of Christ. This supports the prayer’s hope that loss, denial, and hardship can become spiritual gain under God’s hand.
James calls believers to see trials as producing steadfastness and maturity. This grounds the request that testing would not be wasted but would deepen holiness and devotion.

Paul contrasts present affliction with eternal glory and teaches believers to look beyond what is seen. This supports the prayer’s longing for crosses and losses to be transformed by eternal perspective.

provenance.originalAuthor: Unattributed Puritan source (compiled and edited by Arthur Bennett)
provenance.originalSource: The Valley of Vision: A Collection of Puritan Prayers and Devotions, ed. Arthur Bennett (The Banner of Truth Trust)

movements.heading: Asking you to order my path
lines: Lord, your power has no limit, and your wisdom never fails.
Please arrange the details of my life so that they do not block me, discourage me, or get in the way of what you are doing.
Keep me from being dragged into useless conflict.
Protect me from harm, and protect me even more from sin that would twist the gifts, energy, and growth you have given me.
themes: God rules wisely over circumstances
The believer depends on God to remove hindrances and preserve integrity
Spiritual gifts and zeal need protection from corruption by sin

scriptures.connection: This passage calls God’s people to trust his wisdom rather than their own understanding, with the promise that he will make their paths straight. It supports the prayer’s request for God to order the road ahead rather than leaving the believer to self-directed plans.

Peter teaches that gifts are entrusted by God and must be used in dependence on him so that he receives glory. That grounds the concern that even good gifts, zeal, and service must be guarded from sinful misuse.

movements.heading: Keeping me from work you have not given me
lines: Help me do the duty you have actually placed in front of me, not chase some foolish plan of my own.
Do not let me pour myself into work you will not bless.
I want to serve you cleanly, without bringing shame on your name or creating burdens I had no right to take on.
themes: Obedience is better than self-made ambition
God’s blessing matters more than visible activity
Service should be done with integrity and humility

scriptures.connection: Paul says believers are created in Christ for good works that God prepared beforehand. This supports asking to recognize and walk in God-given work rather than inventing self-serving labor.
The psalm teaches that labor apart from the Lord’s building and guarding is ultimately vain. It fits the prayer’s concern not to spend life on work God has not called or blessed.

movements.heading: Hiding under your protection
lines: Let me live close to you, under your shelter.
Be my refuge when danger is obvious and when it is hidden;
when people speak cruelly, when malice is aimed at me, when careless words wound, and when relationships pull me toward sin.
Keep me through the risks of youth, the pressures of middle age, the griefs of old age, and the fear of death.
Father, hold me where I cannot hold myself.
themes: God is the believer’s refuge in visible and invisible dangers
Human life is vulnerable at every stage
The fear of death is brought to God rather than denied

scriptures.connection: The original prayer clearly draws on this psalm’s language of dwelling in God’s shelter amid danger by day and night. The passage supports praying for refuge in God while trusting his protective care.
David speaks of God sheltering his people from human plots and the strife of tongues. This directly illuminates the prayer’s request for protection from malice, slander, and destructive speech.
Hebrews says Christ’s death frees those held in lifelong slavery by the fear of death. That gives gospel depth to the prayer’s plea for courage when facing mortality.

movements.heading: Depending on your Spirit to keep me moving forward
lines: I depend on you completely for strength, wisdom, and comfort.
Uphold me by your Spirit.
But do not let me be satisfied with merely not falling apart or not falling into obvious sin.
Keep me moving forward.
Make me steady, fruitful, and generous in the work you give me to do.
Strengthen me deep inside for every part of following Christ.
themes: The Holy Spirit sustains, counsels, and strengthens believers
Christian perseverance includes growth, not mere survival
God equips his people for faithful work

scriptures.connection: Paul prays that believers would be strengthened with power through the Spirit in the inner person. This closely supports the request for inward strength for the whole Christian life.

Because of Christ’s resurrection, Paul urges believers to be steadfast and always abounding in the Lord’s work. This grounds the prayer’s desire not only to be preserved but to keep advancing in faithful service.

movements.heading: Handing everything back to you
lines: Everything I treasure, I place in your keeping:
my identity in Christ, my body and soul, my abilities, my character, my reputation, my usefulness, my marriage, my children, my friends, my work, today, tomorrow, and the hour when my life ends.
Take all of it.
It already belongs to you.
I belong to you too
now and forever.
themes: The believer’s identity is renewed in Christ
All possessions, relationships, gifts, and the future belong to God
Surrender rests in belonging to the Lord in life and death

scriptures.connection: Paul teaches that whether believers live or die, they belong to the Lord. This supports the prayer’s final entrusting of present life, future, and death to God.
Paul reminds Christians that they are not their own because they were bought with a price. That grounds the prayer’s surrender of body, soul, gifts, and whole life to God.
This passage locates the believer’s life and future hope in Christ. It supports the prayer’s language of a renewed name and identity in Christ, held safely by God.

provenance.adaptationNote: Contemporary prayer based on the theological themes and ideas of the historical source; not a reproduction of the original wording.

movements.heading: Coming before you with honest reverence
lines: Lord, you are eternal, holy, and beyond anything I can fully take in.
Even the angels worship you with awe.
Teach me to come to you with real reverence
not pretending, not careless, not casual about your glory.
Because you are Spirit and you care about truth deep inside me, help me worship you honestly, from the heart, in a way that matches who you are.
themes: God is eternal, holy, and worthy of reverent worship.
True worship is not mere outward form but worship offered in spirit and truth.
God desires inward honesty before him.

scriptures.connection: This passage calls believers to offer worship with reverence and awe because God is holy and consuming. It supports the prayer’s desire to serve God without casualness or presumption.
Jesus teaches that the Father seeks worshipers who worship in spirit and truth. This directly grounds the request for worship that is inwardly honest and spiritually real.
David recognizes that God desires truth in the inner person, not only outward religious expression. That illuminates the prayer’s concern for openness before God at the level of the heart.

movements.heading: Not making room for sin or temporary things
lines: You are righteous, Lord, so please do not let me quietly protect sin in my heart.
Do not let me settle into a worldly frame of mind or look for my deepest satisfaction in things that are already passing away.
Show me where I am attached to what cannot last, and turn my desires back toward you.
themes: God’s righteousness exposes hidden and cherished sin.
Worldly desires are temporary and cannot satisfy the soul.
Repentance includes turning from inward sin and misplaced loves.

scriptures.connection: John contrasts love for the world with love for the Father and says the world is passing away. This supports the prayer’s rejection of worldly-mindedness and satisfaction in perishable things.
The psalmist recognizes the danger of cherishing sin in the heart while approaching God. This grounds the prayer’s request not to harbor hidden sin.

movements.heading: Living now in light of the hour that is coming
lines: I am moving toward the day when so much that feels important now will look small.
On that day it will not finally matter whether I was rich or poor, celebrated or ignored, successful or disappointed.
What will matter is whether I grieved over my sin, longed for righteousness, truly loved the Lord Jesus, and made my boast in his cross.
Father, make these the things I care about most.
themes: Earthly status and achievements are temporary in light of eternity.
God blesses those who mourn sin and hunger for righteousness.
The cross of Christ is the believer’s true boast and central hope.
Sincere love for Jesus matters more than worldly approval or success.

scriptures.connection: Jesus blesses those who mourn and those who hunger and thirst for righteousness. This supports the prayer’s desire for sorrow over sin and deep longing for a righteous life before God.
Paul says his only boast is in the cross of the Lord Jesus Christ. That directly grounds the prayer’s desire to glory in Christ’s cross rather than in earthly success or reputation.
Paul counts former gains as loss compared with knowing Christ and sharing in him. This passage supports the prayer’s reordering of values in light of eternity.

movements.heading: Finding freedom in serving you
lines: Work in me the kind of heart and habits that make obedience to you real freedom.
Change my motives, my loves, and my instincts so that serving you is not a burden I resent, but the life I was made for.
Make me willing, steady, and glad in your ways.
themes: God must form the inner dispositions that lead to faithful service.
Obedience to God is not slavery to misery but freedom from sin.
Christian freedom is found in belonging to God and walking in his ways.

scriptures.connection: Paul describes believers as freed from sin and brought into obedience from the heart. This supports the prayer’s request for inner transformation that makes God’s service true freedom.
The psalmist connects running in God’s commandments with God enlarging the heart. This fits the prayer’s desire for willing, spacious obedience rather than reluctant duty.

movements.heading: Being brave enough to belong to Jesus openly
lines: Drive out the fear and shame that make me hide.
Give me courage to confess Jesus openly before people, even when following him brings criticism or rejection.
Let my zeal be shaped by his knowledge, my choices by his wisdom, and my steps by his careful way of walking in the world.
themes: Believers are called to confess Christ publicly and not be ashamed of him.
Following Jesus can mean bearing reproach with him.
Zeal must be governed by Christ’s wisdom and knowledge, not by pride or impulse.

scriptures.connection: Jesus speaks of acknowledging him before others and warns against denying him. This grounds the prayer’s request for courage to confess the Redeemer openly.

This passage calls believers to go to Jesus outside the camp and bear the reproach associated with him. It supports the prayer’s willingness to identify with Christ even when it costs social acceptance.
Paul presents Christ as the one in whom the treasures of wisdom and knowledge are found. This illuminates the request that zeal and conduct be shaped by Christ’s wisdom rather than mere enthusiasm.

movements.heading: Looking to you for direction, peace, and trust
lines: Teach me to ask you for counsel in everything.
Send me back to Scripture for your direction, and train me to rest my mind in the peace Christ gives.
Help me remember that nothing can touch my life unless it passes through your wise and loving rule.
I do not always understand what you allow, but I want to trust that you are not absent, careless, or overruled.
themes: God gives guidance through prayerful dependence and his Word.
Scripture is the believer’s authoritative direction for faithful living.
Christ gives peace that steadies the mind.
God’s providence governs what happens to his people, even when his purposes are hard to understand.

scriptures.connection: This passage calls for trust in the Lord rather than self-reliance and promises that he directs the path of those who acknowledge him. It supports the prayer’s dependence on God for counsel in all things.
Paul teaches that Scripture is breathed out by God and equips God’s people for every good work. This grounds the prayer’s desire to receive direction from Scripture.
Jesus promises his peace to his disciples in the face of trouble. This supports the request for a mind steadied by Christ’s own peace.

Jesus teaches that even small events fall under the Father’s care and that his people are deeply known by him. This supports the prayer’s trust that nothing befalls the believer apart from God’s providential rule.

movements.heading: Asking for light inside, not just daylight outside
lines: Father of Jesus, morning has come again.
But if your light is not shining in me, the light outside cannot do me real good.
Give me the saving light of your Spirit.
Help me see you clearly as the God who rescues me, the joy of my soul, and the Father who loves me and rejoices over me.
themes: The Holy Spirit gives true spiritual sight.
Outward blessings cannot replace inward grace.
God is not only the believer’s Savior but also the believer’s delight.

scriptures.connection: Paul describes saving knowledge of God as light God shines into the heart through Christ. This grounds the prayer’s request for inward light rather than mere outward brightness.
This passage pictures the Lord delighting in and rejoicing over his people in love. It supports the prayer’s confidence that God’s saving love is not cold or reluctant.

movements.heading: Entrusting my unsafe heart to your care
lines: I place my heart in your hands, because I know how easily it can betray me and how strong its wrong desires can be.
Please guard every doorway of my inner life.
Give me quick discernment when the enemy is working against me.
Help me recognize his lies, even when they look wise, bright, or harmless, and help me resist him and send him away.
themes: The human heart needs God’s guarding care.
Satan deceives, sometimes under the appearance of goodness or truth.
Believers are called to discernment and active resistance.

scriptures.connection: This proverb treats the heart as something that must be watched carefully because the direction of life flows from it. That fits the prayer’s concern for every entrance to the inner life.
Paul warns that Satan can disguise himself as an angel of light. This directly supports the request to detect spiritual danger even when it appears attractive or respectable.
James calls believers to submit to God and resist the devil. The prayer’s desire to reject the enemy is framed not as self-confidence, but as dependence on God.

movements.heading: Let my life make you believable and beautiful to others
lines: Let my words and actions draw other people toward deeper faith and love.
If someone is drifting or lazy in spiritual things, use my example to wake them up.
If someone is living as if this world is all there is, let them see in me that knowing you is better.
If someone is hesitant and undecided about Jesus, let my zeal warn them that judgment is real and Christ is worth running to.
Make me a clear reflection of your grace.
Tune my lips to praise you.
Let kindness shine through the path I walk.
themes: A believer’s life should point others to God’s grace.
Christian example can encourage diligence, repentance, and faith.
Zeal for Christ includes both winsomeness and warning.

scriptures.connection: Jesus teaches that his people’s visible good works should lead others to glorify the Father. This supports the prayer’s desire for words, actions, and kindness to make God attractive to others.
The church is told to stir one another up to love and good works. That gives biblical shape to the request that one person’s example would awaken diligence in others.
Jude holds together mercy toward the wavering and urgent rescue from spiritual danger. This helps frame the prayer’s concern for the timid and undecided without turning warning into harshness.

movements.heading: Doing today’s work with eternity in view
lines: Teach me the glad skill of caring well for ordinary, temporary things while keeping my mind fixed on what lasts forever.
Do not let daily responsibilities pull my heart away from you.
Send me into the world with compassion for people who are confused, wounded, and weighed down.
themes: Christians are to handle earthly responsibilities faithfully without being ruled by them.
Eternal hope should shape ordinary life.
Compassion should move believers toward the needy and spiritually lost.

scriptures.connection: Paul tells believers to set their minds on things above because their life is hidden with Christ. This supports the prayer’s desire to live in the present with an eternal center of gravity.
Jesus sees the crowds with compassion because they are harassed and helpless. The prayer’s request to be sent toward the ignorant and miserable reflects Christ’s own posture toward needy people.

movements.heading: Walking like Jesus in humility and meekness
lines: Help me walk as Jesus walked.
He is my only Savior and my perfect pattern.
Let his mind take hold of my inner life.
Let his meekness be what people see covering me.
Make me at home among the poor in spirit, and let me gladly take my place with the meek.
Teach me to count others as more important than myself.
Let me find in true humility the inheritance you give now and the inheritance still to come.
themes: Jesus is both Savior and the pattern for Christian holiness.
Christlike humility means valuing others above self.
The meek and poor in spirit receive God’s kingdom and future inheritance.

scriptures.connection: John says those who claim to abide in Christ ought to walk as he walked. This directly grounds the prayer’s desire for practical Christlikeness.

Paul commands believers to count others more significant than themselves and points to Christ’s humility as the model. This supports the prayer’s movement from Christ’s mind to humble treatment of others.
Jesus blesses the poor in spirit and the meek, promising the kingdom and the earth. This illuminates the prayer’s language about finding a true inheritance in humility.

provenance.adaptationNote: Contemporary prayer based on the theological themes and ideas of the historical source; not a reproduction of the original wording.

movements.heading: Admitting I cannot love as you command
lines: Father, you call me to love you with everything I am
my heart, my desires, my thoughts, my strength
and to love my neighbor as I love myself.
I know this is right, and I want it to be true of me.
But I also know I do not have this kind of love in myself.
Left to myself, my loves bend away from you.
I get tangled up in cravings, self-protection, pride, and comfort.
You are completely worthy of my love, but I cannot give you pure love unless you rescue and free my heart.
themes: God commands wholehearted love for himself and genuine love for neighbor.
Human love is disordered by sin and cannot make itself pure without God’s freeing grace.
Confession of moral inability is not an excuse but an honest dependence on God.

scriptures.connection: Jesus identifies love for God and love for neighbor as the heart of God’s commandments. This grounds the prayer’s opening desire to love God wholly and people rightly.
Paul teaches that the mind set on the flesh is hostile to God and cannot submit to him. That supports the prayer’s confession that natural affections, apart from grace, do not freely love God.

movements.heading: Standing in the freedom Jesus has given me
lines: Thank you that, by your grace, I am no longer owned by sin.
I belong to you.
I believe you are my God because of Jesus, and through him you have bought me back, forgiven my sins, and made me free to serve you.
I do not want freedom so I can live for myself.
I want to obey you as your redeemed child.
themes: Freedom from sin comes through Christ, not self-improvement.
Redemption and forgiveness create willing service to God.
Christian obedience flows from grace, not from an attempt to earn acceptance.

scriptures.connection: This passage joins redemption through Christ’s blood with the forgiveness of sins according to God’s grace. It directly supports the prayer’s confidence that forgiveness and freedom are received through Jesus.
Paul describes Christ as the one who sets his people free. The prayer’s desire to serve God as a freed person rests on that gospel freedom rather than on self-generated righteousness.

movements.heading: Depending on your Spirit to walk in that freedom
lines: Lord, the same way I could not free myself in the beginning, I cannot live faithfully now by my own strength.
Please let your Spirit draw me close to you, make your ways attractive to me, and teach me to walk in the freedom you have already given.
Keep me from treating your grace as something I can carry without you.
themes: The Christian life continues by dependence on the Spirit.
Obedience is the fruit of grace, not the achievement of independent strength.
True liberty is walking with God, not self-rule.

scriptures.connection: Paul warns that Christian freedom is not an opening for self-indulgence but a call to love and to walk by the Spirit. This fits the prayer’s request to live freely in obedience rather than return to bondage.
Jesus teaches that his disciples can bear fruit only by abiding in him. The prayer’s dependence on God for ongoing obedience reflects that same need for continual life from Christ.

movements.heading: Using your Word to bring me to you
lines: Father, keep every practice, habit, and help in my life pointed toward you.
If something does not lead me nearer to you, it will leave me empty no matter how religious it looks.
Shape my steps by your Word.
Teach me to receive your commands not as a burden but as a path into fellowship with you.
Make obedience a place where I meet you, hear you, and learn to enjoy you.
themes: Spiritual means are valuable because they lead to communion with God.
Scripture orders the believer’s life and directs the heart toward God.
God’s commandments are meant to become joy, not mere external pressure.

scriptures.connection: The psalmist asks God to lead him in the path of God’s commandments and turn his heart away from worthless things. This supports the prayer’s desire for God’s Word to order life and make obedience joyful.
Jesus connects love for him with keeping his commandments and with his self-disclosure to the believer. That grounds the prayer’s hope that obedience can be real fellowship with God.

movements.heading: Making me love people with the love of Jesus
lines: Spirit of love, grow your love in me and let it become visible in the way I treat people.
Make me more like Jesus
not only in what I say I believe, but in the kindness I show, the good I do, the patience I practice, and the mercy I offer.
Let people see something of your goodness in my life, so that the honor goes to you and not to me.
themes: God’s love in the believer should become visible love toward others.
Christ is the pattern for Christian compassion and active goodness.
Good works are meant to glorify God, not the person doing them.

scriptures.connection: Jesus commands his disciples to love one another as he has loved them and says this love will mark them as his disciples. This directly supports the prayer’s request to become loving in a recognizably Christlike way.
Jesus teaches that visible good works should lead others to glorify the Father. That fits the prayer’s desire for love and service to shine before others without stealing God’s honor.

movements.heading: Keeping me humble when you work through me
lines: And Father, the more you work in me and through me, the more humble I need to become.
Do not let love make me proud, as if it came from me.
Keep me gentle, low, teachable, and quick to give you the credit.
If there is any good in me, it is your gift.
If any good comes through me, it is your work.
Let that truth keep me close to the ground and close to you.
themes: Spiritual fruit should deepen humility, not pride.
All good in the believer comes from God’s grace and power.
God receives the honor for the love he produces in and through his people.

scriptures.connection: Paul challenges boasting by reminding believers that everything they have is received. This supports the prayer’s refusal to take credit for love or usefulness that comes from God.
Paul says God works in believers both to will and to work for his good pleasure. That grounds the prayer’s confession that any loving desire or action is ultimately God’s work in the believer.

provenance.originalAuthor: Unattributed Puritan source (compiled and edited by Arthur Bennett)
provenance.originalSource: The Valley of Vision: A Collection of Puritan Prayers and Devotions, ed. Arthur Bennett (The Banner of Truth Trust)
provenance.copyrightStatus: Compilation, titles and arrangement in copyright (Banner of Truth, 1975); underlying Puritan sources are public domain.
