movements.heading: Coming to you for what only you can give
lines: Lord God, every good thing we truly need is in your hands.
Nothing we ask in your will is beyond your power, and you have already shown your generosity to crowds of people as undeserving and guilty as we are.
Help us stop acting as if we have to earn your help or manage without you.
Make us willing to receive from your kindness, honestly and gratefully, as needy people coming to a generous Father.
themes: God is able and willing to give what his people need.
Grace is received by the undeserving, not earned by the worthy.
Believers come to God as dependent children, trusting his bounty.

scriptures.connection: Paul grounds Christian confidence in God's greatest gift: he did not spare his own Son. If God has given Christ, his people can trust him to supply every lesser mercy according to his will.
Jesus teaches his disciples to ask their Father for what they need because the Father gives good gifts. This supports the prayer’s movement from neediness to confident dependence on God’s generosity.

movements.heading: Letting the truth about our sin reach us
lines: To make us ready to receive your mercy, show us the truth about ourselves.
Convince us of our sin.
Soften hearts that have become hard.
Teach us to grieve over our foolishness, our ingratitude, our pride, our unbelief, our rebellion, and the corruption that still clings to us.
Let your law expose us so clearly that we stop trying to justify ourselves by it.
Then turn our eyes, with wonder and glad surrender, to the salvation you have provided in Christ, for the glory of your name and the rescue of sinners like us.
themes: God’s law exposes sin and shuts down self-justification.
True repentance includes grief over sin and a softened heart.
Salvation is God’s provision in Christ, displaying his glory in mercy and justice.

scriptures.connection: This passage shows the law’s work in silencing human boasting and revealing guilt, then announces God’s righteousness given through faith in Christ. It directly supports the prayer’s move from conviction to wonder at God’s saving provision.

Paul speaks of dying to the law in order to live to God, with life now centered on the Son of God who loved him and gave himself for him. This illuminates the prayer’s request to stop relying on law-keeping and to look to Christ.

movements.heading: Give us hope, love, joy, and faith that keep going
lines: Give us a hope that will not embarrass us in the end, because it rests on you.
Give us love that does not stay in our feelings but moves us into real obedience.
Give us joy in you that strengthens us when our own strength is thin.
Give us faith in your Son, who loved us and gave himself for us.
And when we do not feel your nearness clearly, keep us faithful anyway.
Help us keep doing the duties you have given us, wait for you, walk in your way, and pray humbly and earnestly at your feet.
Keep eternity close enough in our minds that we do not waste the life you have entrusted to us.
themes: Christian hope rests on God’s proven love and will not finally disappoint.
Love for God expresses itself in obedience.
Faith continues in duty even when God’s presence is not strongly felt.
Awareness of eternity shapes faithful living now.

scriptures.connection: Paul connects justification, suffering, endurance, character, and hope, and says this hope does not put believers to shame because God’s love has been poured into their hearts. This grounds the prayer for enduring, confident hope.

Jesus links love for him with keeping his commandments. The prayer’s request for a love that leads to holy obedience reflects this relationship between affection for Christ and practical faithfulness.

Hebrews urges believers not to throw away their confidence but to endure and live by faith. This supports the prayer for perseverance when spiritual feeling is weak and obedience must continue by trust.

movements.heading: Putting our lives back in your hands
lines: Place us at your disposal for whatever duties and events you appoint.
Teach us to bring our preferences under your wisdom and your will.
If you ask us to give up comforts or enjoyments we would rather keep, help us surrender them without accusing you.
You are not only our rightful Lord;
you are our truest Friend.
So make us willing to belong to you completely, trusting that your way is wiser and kinder than ours.
themes: God has rightful authority over his people as Creator and Redeemer.
Surrender means submitting preferences, plans, and comforts to God’s wise will.
God’s lordship is not cold ownership but faithful, loving friendship in Christ.

scriptures.connection: Paul urges believers, in view of God’s mercies, to offer themselves wholly to God and be transformed rather than shaped by the world. This supports the prayer’s surrender of the whole life to God’s will.
James corrects self-confident planning by reminding believers that life is dependent on the Lord’s will. This connects with submitting our preferences and future events to God’s wisdom.

Jesus calls his disciples friends and defines that friendship through his self-giving love and revealed will. This helps hold together the prayer’s language of God’s authority and his personal kindness toward us.

movements.heading: Receiving grace through worship and the Lord’s Day
lines: Even after all the ways we have provoked you and failed you, make us thankful for the ordinary ways you keep giving us grace:
your Word, prayer, gathered worship, fellowship, and the signs and practices you have given your church.
Teach us to benefit from them more than we have.
As we come to the Lord’s Day, help us not drift into it carelessly.
Make us spiritually awake to its seriousness, its responsibilities, and its gifts.
Help us set aside what can be set aside, turn from needless distraction, and worship you with our minds and hearts.
Let us know the happiness of people whose strength is in you, whose hearts are set on the road that leads home to you.
themes: God strengthens believers through ordinary means of grace and gathered worship.
The Lord’s Day is received as a gift and responsibility for worship and spiritual renewal.
True blessedness belongs to those whose strength is in God and whose hearts are set toward him.

scriptures.connection: The early church devoted itself to apostolic teaching, fellowship, the breaking of bread, and prayers. This provides a biblical picture of the ordinary means by which God nourishes his people together.

Hebrews calls believers not to neglect meeting together but to encourage one another toward love and good works. This supports the prayer’s gratitude for gathered worship and its desire to profit more from it.

John identifies being in the Spirit on the Lord’s Day, giving biblical language for spiritual attentiveness on the day associated with the risen Lord. The prayer draws on that language without reducing it to mere formal observance.

Psalm 84 blesses those whose strength is in God and whose hearts are set on pilgrimage toward him. This directly supports the prayer’s closing desire to find strength in God on the way to his presence.
